thread.title: Stocks See Further Downside After Early Slump

author: rttnews.com
title: Stocks See Further Downside After Early Slump
text:
After coming under pressure early in the session, stocks have seen further downside over the course of the trading day on Monday. The major averages have slid firmly into negative territory, with the Dow continuing to give back ground after reaching its best closing level in a month last Thursday.
In recent trading, the major averages have climbed off their lows of the session, but they continue to post steep losses. The Dow is down 404.29 points or 1.6 percent at 25,585.01, the Nasdaq is down 169.23 points or 2.3 percent at 7,237.67 and the S&P 500 is down 38.45 points or 1.4 percent at 2,742.56.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple (AAPL) is weighing on Wall Street, with the tech giant tumbling by 4.4 percent to its lowest intraday level in over three months.
The steep drop by Apple comes after iPhone parts supplier Lumentum cut its fiscal second quarter guidance, adding to recent concerns about iPhone demand.
Industrial conglomerate General Electric (GE) has also moved significantly lower after Chairman and CEO Larry Culp told CNBC he feels the "urgency" to reduce the company's leverage and will do so through asset sales.
Concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates are also contributing to the sell-off on Wall Street.
Light trading activity may be exaggerating the downward momentum, however, as government offices, the bond markets , and most banks are closed in observance of Veterans Day.
A lack of major U.S. economic data is also keeping some traders on the sidelines ahead of the release of reports on consumer price inflation, retail sales, and industrial production in the coming days.
A speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Wednesday is also likely to attract attention, as traders look for additional clues about the outlook for interest rates.
Last week, the Fed left interest rates unchanged as widely expected but indicated it remains on track to gradually raise rates despite signs of a slowdown in the pace of growth in business investment.
Sector News
Semiconductor stocks continue to see substantial weakness in mid-day trading, resulting in a 4.1 percent nosedive by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.
Within the semiconductor sector, Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) is posting a steep loss after Citi downgraded its rating on the Apple chip supplier's stock to Neutral from Buy.
Significant weakness has also emerged among oil service stocks, as reflected by the 2.7 percent slump by the Philadelphia Oil Service Index. The index is on pace to end the session at a more than nine-year closing low.
The sell-off by oil service stocks comes despite a rebound by the price of crude oil, as crude for December delivery is climbing $0.71 to $60.90 a barrel after ending last Friday's trading at its lowest closing level since March.
Computer hardware, biotechnology, and software stocks are also seeing considerable weakness, contributing to the steep drop by the tech-heavy Nasdaq.
Most of the other major sectors have also moved to the downside on the day, with notable weakness visible among retail, tobacco, and brokerage stocks.
Other Markets
In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Monday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index and Index both inched up by 0.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index shot up by 1.2 percent.
Meanwhile, the major European markets showed notable moves to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index plunged by 1.8 percent, the French CAC 40 Index and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index dropped by 0.9 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
Treasuries moved notably higher during the trading session last Friday, but the bond markets are closed on the day in observance of Veterans Day.
